verses.text: Look, you are beautiful, my love. Look, you are beautiful. Your eyes behind your veil are like doves. Your hair is like a flock of goats coming down from Mount Gilead.
Your teeth are like a flock of sheep just shorn, coming up from the washing. Each one has its twin, and not one of them is missing.
Your lips are like a scarlet thread, and your mouth is lovely. Your cheeks behind your veil are like halves of a pomegranate.
Your neck is like the tower of David, built to store weapons, with a thousand shields hanging on it, all the shields of strong warriors.
Your two breasts are like two fawns, twins of a gazelle, feeding among the lilies.
Until the day cools and the shadows run away, I will go to the mountain of myrrh and to the hill of frankincense.
You are beautiful in every way, my love. There is no flaw in you.
Come with me from Lebanon, my bride, come with me from Lebanon. Look down from the top of Amana, from the tops of Senir and Hermon, from the dens of the lions and the mountains of the leopards.
You have stolen my heart, my sister, my bride. You have stolen my heart with one look of your eyes, with one jewel of your necklace.
How beautiful is your love, my sister, my bride! Your love is so much better than wine, and the smell of your perfume is better than any spice!
Your lips, my bride, drip sweetness like honey from the comb. Honey and milk are under your tongue. The smell of your clothes is like the smell of Lebanon.
My sister, my bride, you are a garden locked up, a spring closed up, a sealed fountain.
Your plants are an orchard of pomegranates with the finest fruits, with henna and nard,
nard and saffron, calamus and cinnamon, with every kind of incense tree, myrrh and aloes, and all the finest spices.
You are a fountain in the gardens, a well of fresh flowing water, streams flowing down from Lebanon.
Wake up, north wind, and come, south wind! Blow on my garden, so that its sweet smells spread. Let my beloved come into his garden and taste its finest fruits.
